acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Djinn family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Djinn, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Ring-Vector Specialist (Specialist) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Sharply defined figure with ornate sashes and jewelry, arms of visibly swirling wind, and gold rings orbiting the forearms.
Signature mechanic: Three-Wish Vector: three gold rings align around one visible wind forearm, then release pressure lanes in outer-to-inner order while the other arm stays still.
battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a directional controller that separates visible wind-arm direction from orbiting-ring release order.
constructionDimensions: Material/structure branches: T1 vapor, half-face, and trailing plume gain a mineral boundary clamp; T2 the defined torso and plain cuffs gain crystal load keys; T3 visible wind arms and orbiting rings gain sediment weights; T4 crown and sacred script gain fractured anchor glyphs; T5 vortex, throne, and lamps gain bounded throne braces.

Motion/process branches: T1 the vapor half-face briefly loads the plume clamp while hovering; T2 the torso transfers weight through one cuff key; T3 the wind arms alternate orbiting-ring loads; T4 crown script commits one anchor glyph; T5 vortex, throne, and lamps load and release one throne brace.
counterplay: Move through the still arm's lane and strike the widest ring gap before the inner release. Affinity signal: Affinity counterplay branches: T1 the vapor half-face exposes its plume-clamp fault after the brief load; T2 the torso cuff exposes its crystal key after transfer; T3 wind arms and orbiting rings expose the weighted load gap after release; T4 crown script exposes the fractured anchor glyph after commitment; T5 vortex, throne, and lamps expose the throne brace when its load releases.
identityInvariants: A hovering humanoid upper body tapers into smoke instead of legs; solidity and scale change only at explicit tiers.
Sapphire or violet smoke, warm inner light, gold, brass, turquoise, silk, and gemstones remain distinct source materials.
Cuffs, rings, headpieces, lamps, and script mark proposed binding status without establishing universal culture or morality.
The body becomes less solid and more spatially dominant from half-face vapor to a palace-scale throne vortex.
telegraph: Ornate sash tails stream in one direction and the three forearm rings click into visibly unequal spacing.
